clue.text: Like supporter at home holding a kind of sign inside boundary

parts.note: at home means in, as in 'staying in'

indicators.note: inside places the sign and its article within the cricket boundary

parts.note: a four is a cricket boundary hit along the ground
V is the sign for versus, or the V-sign

explanation.surface: A home fan holds up a placard at the edge of the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a four is a boundary hit that reaches the rope after bouncing; 'inside' places the article and the versus sign within it.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone in favour of a cause backs it, just as a supporter does.

clue.text: Bachelor with one diamond, say, for movie actress

parts.note: one can be the indefinite article a
a bid of diamonds in bridge is an example of a call

explanation.surface: A single man with one diamond hopes to woo a film star.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Diamond' suggests a jewel, but in bridge a bid such as one diamond is a call.
explanation.definitionFit: Lauren Bacall was a Hollywood film star of the 1940s and 50s, so she exemplifies a movie actress.

clue.text: I am holding pine up over a shrub

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means the first part sits above what follows
in a down clue, up means the whole container is read bottom to top
holding puts the yearning word between the two little words

parts.note: taken as written, the two words I and AM
to pine is to long for something

explanation.surface: Someone clutches a pine sapling above a garden bush.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding' puts LONG inside I AM to make ILONGAM; 'up' turns that to MAGNOLI, and 'over' puts it above A. Magnolias are often trees, a point the blog commenters raised.
explanation.definitionFit: Magnolias are flowering woody plants, some grown as bushes, so a shrub is a fair example class.

clue.text: Take part in ruling over nation

definitions.text: Take part in ruling over nation

indicators.note: take part in tells us to take a part of the following words, a run within them

explanation.surface: An instruction to join in the business of running a country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take part in' signals a run of letters inside 'ruling over nation'; the whole clue doubles as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To take part in ruling a country is to exercise political control over it, the core sense of the verb.

clue.text: Vessel crossing area, following a straight course

indicators.note: the ship crosses the area, so it goes around and through the letter

parts.note: a liner is a large passenger ship

explanation.surface: A ship crosses a stretch of sea on a direct heading.
explanation.definitionFit: Linear describes something arranged along a straight line, like a direct route.

clue.text: American author who chronicled abysmal conditions in this city

definitions.meaning: Jack ..., the American novelist of The Call of the Wild

definitions.text: who chronicled abysmal conditions in this city
definitions.meaning: the same writer's The People of the Abyss (1903) described the poverty of the East End of the British capital

explanation.walkthrough: 'abysmal' nods to the book title The People of the Abyss; the city is the one the author wrote about, sharing his surname.
explanation.definitionFit: Jack London both bears the surname and wrote about the capital's slums, so writer and city share the name.

clue.text: Arrangement wherein you must come in behind, but not last

indicators.note: must come in places the pronoun inside the shortened word
but not last drops the final letter of the word for behind

parts.note: behind schedule means late

explanation.surface: Instructions for a queue: you must join at the back, but not as the very last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'but not last' trims the word for behind by its final letter, and 'must come in' sets the pronoun inside what remains; 'wherein' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A layout is the way things are set out, which is an arrangement.

clue.text: In charge, European is maximally loyal

indicators.note: In places the European letter inside the word for charge

parts.note: something in your charge is in your trust or care

explanation.surface: A European in charge is the most loyal of all.
explanation.definitionFit: Truest is the superlative of true, and true means faithful, so it is the most faithful.

clue.text: Person taking lead runs inside to take care of dog

indicators.note: inside places the runs letter within the word for caring

parts.note: to tend is to take care of
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
a setter is a breed of gundog

explanation.surface: Someone holding a lead hurries indoors to look after the dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking lead' suggests a dog lead, but it means being a leader of fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: A trendsetter leads others by starting fashions they follow.

clue.text: Kept in mind a banking conference in Africa

indicators.note: kept in says the letters are held within the following words

explanation.surface: Someone remembered a bank's meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: An indaba is a Zulu-derived word for a council or meeting in southern Africa.

clue.text: Messed around with English in ten poems

indicators.note: messed means jumbled, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: X is the Roman numeral for ten

explanation.surface: Someone fooled about with English while writing ten verses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Messed' looks like part of the phrase 'messed around', but it is the anagram signal working on 'around' plus E; the Roman ten then follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Rondeaux is the plural of rondeau, a French verse form with a refrain, so these are poems.

clue.text: Thomas, for example, holding clubs in card game

indicators.note: holding means the card game contains the suit letter

parts.note: loo is an old card game
C is the abbreviation for clubs in card games

explanation.surface: A man named Thomas grips his clubs in a game of cards.
explanation.walkthrough: Thomas is Thomas the Tank Engine, the children's-book steam engine; LOO is a card game popular in Victorian Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas the Tank Engine is a fictional railway engine, which loco abbreviates.

clue.text: With learner getting punishment at school in my isolated state

parts.note: L is for learner, as on L-plates

indicators.note: in places the school penalty within the possessive word

parts.note: one's can stand for my, as in 'to one's cost'
lines are sentences a pupil is made to copy out as a penalty

explanation.surface: A pupil is given a punishment and left on their own.
explanation.walkthrough: 'my' stands for the impersonal possessive one's, as in 'to one's cost'; 'in' places the school penalty inside it, with the learner letter in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Loneliness is the condition of being alone and cut off from others.

clue.text: Gets out of line, as today's solution does in every other row

definitions.meaning: to step out of a formation or defy discipline

definitions.text: as today's solution does in every other row
definitions.meaning: in alternate grid rows, pairs of entries are formed by splitting a rank such as EARL, BARON, COLONEL or ENSIGN across them

explanation.walkthrough: The theme: in every other row, a rank name runs across adjacent entries, so the ranks are broken.
explanation.definitionFit: Breaking ranks means leaving a formation, which is getting out of line.

clue.text: Features of many crosswords, for example, reappear in two words

definitions.meaning: rearrangements of letters used as wordplay

definitions.text: for example, reappear in two words
definitions.meaning: split into two words, reappear gives REAP and PEAR, which are rearrangements of each other

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition gives an example: split REAPPEAR into REAP and PEAR and each is the other rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Rearranged-letter words are the staple wordplay of cryptic puzzles, and REAP and PEAR are one such pair.

clue.text: Asian type somehow making his mark on India

indicators.note: somehow says the letters are arranged in some unstated way

parts.note: I is India in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Some Asian person has made his mark on India.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somehow' rearranges HISMARK into KASHMIR, then I goes below it in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A Kashmiri is a native of Kashmir, a region of South Asia.

clue.text: Bishop or knight taking rook or queen to force a way through

indicators.note: taking means the piece takes in, or contains, the letter

parts.note: either is a chess piece
R stands for rook in chess notation and for regina, queen

explanation.surface: A chess move where a minor piece captures a rook or queen to break through.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rook or queen' works either way: R is rook in chess notation and R (regina) is queen.
explanation.definitionFit: To pierce is to penetrate, pushing a way through something.

clue.text: A sin that's done!

parts.note: greed is one of the seven deadly sins

explanation.surface: An exclamation that a sin has been committed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's done' reads as a sin committed, but 'Done!' is the cry that settles a deal.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying 'Done!' accepts a bargain, the same as saying it is settled by consent.

clue.text: Take the stuffing out of food devoured without resistance

parts.note: a dish is a prepared food

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the devoured word surrounds the letter

parts.note: devoured means eaten
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A dish was wolfed down with no one resisting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking', but here means outside: EATEN goes round R.
explanation.definitionFit: To dishearten someone is to deflate them, knocking the fight out of them.

clue.text: In a frenzy, check it out, with no end of work

indicators.note: out signals that the letters are put out of order
with no removes a letter from the pair of words
end of picks the last letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: Someone frantically checks their work, unable to finish it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'end of work' is K; 'with no' takes it from CHECKIT, leaving CHECIT, which 'out' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Hectic means frantic and full of feverish activity.

clue.text: Crazy name, say

definitions.note: used as a noun, a crazy is a madman, matching this noun

parts.note: to utter is to say

explanation.surface: A request to give a mad name.
explanation.definitionFit: A nutter is slang for a madman, someone wildly eccentric.

clue.text: Warning evil's masking good

indicators.note: masking means the sin covers or encloses the letter

parts.note: evil means sin

explanation.surface: A caution that wickedness hides behind goodness.
explanation.definitionFit: A sign can be an omen or portent, a warning of what is coming.

clue.text: Eccentric rector in old hat

indicators.note: eccentric means odd, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An odd clergyman wearing antiquated headgear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old hat' reads as 'out of date', but it is a literal hat of an older age.
explanation.definitionFit: A tricorne is a three-cornered hat worn in the 18th century.

clue.text: Moderate or strong show of irritation

definitions.meaning: to moderate is to tone down or soften
a fit of anger or rage

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to soften or tone down, while the noun is an outburst of anger.

clue.text: Altered image about me, finally, in this puzzle

indicators.note: about means the rearranged word goes round the letter
altered means changed, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: me is the setter, Brendan, whose final letter is N

explanation.surface: A self-portrait has been changed and the setter appears in the puzzle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Altered' turns IMAGE into EIGMA; 'about' puts it round N, the last letter of BRENDAN, the setter, who is 'me'.
explanation.definitionFit: An enigma is a riddle or mystery, and a crossword is a kind of puzzle.

clue.text: Tips for trombone joining a kind of jazz quartet

indicators.note: the tips of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: trad is traditional jazz, the revivalist New Orleans style

explanation.surface: A trombonist joins a traditional jazz four-piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A tetrad is a group of four, the same idea as a quartet.
